title: Revocation snapshot
description: The tenant's live revoked sessions, bounded so the body always fits the reader's cap. `complete` says the body carries the whole live set; `truncated` says the opposite. A module that is told the body is incomplete adds to its local set and keeps what it has — replacing it would un-revoke the sessions the body did not carry.

revision.description: The tenant's revision of its live revoked set. It advances whenever the set changes — a new revocation or a restore — and is 0 while nothing is revoked.

complete.description: True when the body carries the tenant's entire live revoked set.

truncated.description: The same fact from the other side: true when the set did not fit and the body is a bounded prefix of it.

revoked_sessions.description: The live revoked session ids, newest first. A flat array of ids, so a module that predates the bounded snapshot still reads it.

revocations.description: The same revocations, each with the agent id and the revocation time. The ledger's revocation key is (tenant_id, agent_id, session_id), so the session id alone does not identify a revocation.
